---
title: "Apparent micronutrient intake and fortification scenarios from a household consumption and expenditure survey"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
params:
  lang: "en"
  country: "Exampleland (invented data)"
  survey: "hces_example, the synthetic survey of hcesfort"
  year: 2026
  nutrients: ["iron", "folate", "vitamin_a"]
  reference_scenario: "flour"
  domains: ["region", "expenditure_group"]
  equity_domain: "expenditure_group"
  min_n: 10
  max_half_width: 0.15
  min_coverage: 0.8
  min_records_used: 0.8
  iron_bioavailability: 0.10
  iron_bioavailability_sensitivity: [0.05, 0.15]
  level: 0.95
  lonely_psu: "adjust"
  raw_coverage_threshold: null
---

<!--
Report template of hcesfort (use_report_template()). Every number comes
from _results.R; every sentence that states a finding is built by
_headlines.R and stops the render when the data no longer support it.
Replace the ADAPTER block of _results.R with your survey, set the params
above, edit actions.csv and decisions.csv, and write the prose marked
"Analyst:". Design: docs/design-report-template.md of the package.
-->

```{r setup}
source("_results.R", local = TRUE)
source("_headlines.R", local = TRUE)
source("_figures.R", local = TRUE)
lang <- p$lang
lev <- p$level
top_nutrient <- q1$nutrient[q1$scenario == p$reference_scenario][
  which.max(q1$estimate[q1$scenario == p$reference_scenario])
]
top_column <- nutrients$column[nutrients$nutrient == top_nutrient]
h <- list(
  q1 = headline_q1(q1, p$reference_scenario, lev, lang),
  q2 = headline_q2(q2, top_nutrient, p$domains[[1]], lang),
  q3 = headline_q3(q3, top_column, top_nutrient, lev, lang),
  q4 = headline_q4(q4, lev, lang),
  q5 = headline_q5(q5, lev, lang),
  q6 = headline_q6(q6, lev, lang)
)
n_est <- sum(intake$intake_status == "estimated")
records_used <- sum(intake$n_records_used) / sum(intake$n_records_included)
```

**Survey:** `r p$survey`. **Country:** `r p$country`. **Year:** `r p$year`.

## The answer in one page

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| [Q1](#q1) Which micronutrients have the greatest risk of inadequate intake? | `r h$q1` |
| [Q2](#q2) Which population groups are most at risk? | `r h$q2` |
| [Q3](#q3) Which foods supply each key micronutrient? | `r h$q3` |
| [Q4](#q4) How far does each fortification vehicle reach? | `r h$q4` |
| [Q5](#q5) Who is left outside the reach of the vehicles? | `r h$q5` |
| [Q6](#q6) What would each fortification scenario change? | `r h$q6` |

::: {.callout-note}
## How to read these figures
**Apparent intake** is the food a household acquires, converted to
nutrients and divided among its members by their energy needs (adult
female equivalents). It is **not** individual intake and **not** a measure
of deficiency. Gains from fortification are **potential**: they assume
the compliance stated in each scenario.
:::

**Fitness for use.** `r n_est` of `r nrow(intake)` households have an
estimate and `r pct(records_used)` of the included food records were used.
The comparison between scenarios is more robust than the absolute level;
the conditions are in [Q7](#q7).

## Which micronutrients have the greatest risk of inadequate intake? {#q1}

**`r h$q1`**

```{r q1-figure}
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-cap: "Households below the requirement, by nutrient: the unfortified baseline and the reference scenario. Hollow dots: low precision. Source: inadequacy(), estimate_households(), flag_precision()."
fig_dot(q1, "nutrient", "Households at risk of inadequate intake",
        colour = "scenario")
```

Iron by the probability approach with a bioavailability of
`r pct(p$iron_bioavailability)`; the other nutrients by the EAR cut-point.
Nutrients that fail the coverage minimum (`r pct(p$min_coverage)`) appear
as not estimated, never dropped. *Analyst: one to three sentences on the
nutritional relevance of the finding.*

## Which population groups are most at risk? (exploratory) {#q2}

**`r h$q2`**

```{r q2-figure}
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Households at risk under the reference scenario, by domain. Hollow dots: low precision. Exploratory comparisons, no test between domains. Source: estimate_households(by = ), flag_precision()."
fig_dot(q2, "domain_value", "Households at risk of inadequate intake",
        colour = "nutrient", facet = "domain")
```

These comparisons are exploratory: `r nrow(q2)` estimates across
`r length(p$domains)` domain variables, without a test between domains.
The same figure for recorded energy is in [annex D](#annex-d).

## Which foods supply each key micronutrient? {#q3}

**`r h$q3`**

```{r q3-figure}
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Share of each food group in the apparent intake per adult female equivalent, before fortification (unfortified baseline). Source: food_group_intake(), food_group_shares()."
fig_dot(q3, "food_group", "Share of the nutrient in the apparent diet",
        facet = "variable")
```

Shares are computed on the unfortified baseline, so enriched foods count
without what enrichment added. Foods without a group are shown as
`unclassified`.

## How far does each fortification vehicle reach? {#q4}

**`r h$q4`**

```{r q4-figure}
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-cap: "Households that acquire each vehicle (the first stage of coverage, the only one a household survey observes). Source: vehicle_coverage(), estimate_households(value = \"acquired\")."
g <- fig_dot(q4[q4$level != "combined", ], "vehicle",
             "Households that acquire the vehicle", colour = "level")
if (!is.null(p$raw_coverage_threshold)) {
  g <- g + geom_vline(xintercept = p$raw_coverage_threshold, linetype = 2)
}
g
```

```{r q4-table}
qty <- as.data.frame(q4_qty)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(vehicle = qty$vehicle,
             median_g = round(qty$estimate, 1),
             ci = paste0(round(qty$ci_low, 1), "–",
                         round(qty$ci_high, 1)),
             n = qty$n),
  col.names = c("Vehicle", "Median g per AFE and day",
                paste0(pct(lev), " CI"), "Households"),
  caption = "Quantity among the households that acquire the vehicle only. Source: estimate_households(statistic = \"median\", domain = \"acquired\")."
)
```

## Who is left outside the reach of the vehicles? (exploratory) {#q5}

**`r h$q5`**

```{r q5-table}
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(domain = q5$domain, group = q5$domain_value,
             none = pct(q5$none),
             ci = ifelse(is.na(q5$ci_low), "—",
                         paste0(pct(q5$ci_low), "–", pct(q5$ci_high))),
             n = q5$n),
  col.names = c("Domain", "Group", "Acquire no vehicle",
                paste0(pct(lev), " CI"), "Households"),
  caption = "Households that acquire none of the vehicles. Source: vehicle_coverage(combine = ), estimate_households(by = )."
)
```

## What would each fortification scenario change? {#q6}

**`r h$q6`**

```{r q6-scenarios}
knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(scenarios)[c("scenario", "vehicle", "nutrient", "level_mg_kg",
                             "level_basis", "compliance", "source")],
  caption = "Fortification scenarios as modelled. Source: the scenarios table."
)
```

```{r q6-figure}
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: "Paired change in the share of households at risk, each action against its comparator (actions.csv). Source: estimate_difference()."
fig_dot(q6, "nutrient", "Change in households at risk (proportion)",
        colour = "action", percent = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2)
```

```{r q6-equity}
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Paired change by the equity domain (exploratory). Rows only for the nutrients each action changes. Source: estimate_difference(by = )."
q6_equity$label <- paste(q6_equity$action, q6_equity$nutrient, sep = ": ")
fig_dot(q6_equity, p$equity_domain, "Change in households at risk (proportion)",
        colour = "label", percent = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2)
```

```{r q6-ul}
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-cap: "Households above the upper level, on the form the upper level applies to. Source: above_ul(), estimate_households()."
fig_dot(q6_ul, "nutrient", "Households above the upper level",
        colour = "scenario")
```

A gain is read together with the households it would take above the
upper level. *Analyst: one to three sentences.*

## What can these figures not answer, and what is needed next? {#q7}

**The comparison between scenarios is more robust than the absolute
level.**

```{r q7-decisions}
knitr::kable(decisions, caption = "Decisions that condition the interpretation (decisions.csv, written by the analyst).")
```

Pre-filled from the chain: requirements from the `requirements` table
(annex F); iron bioavailability `r pct(p$iron_bioavailability)`;
compliance as stated in each scenario; `r pct(records_used)` of the
included records used (annex B).

Open questions: measured compliance of the fortified foods; validation
against individual intake or biomarkers; the next survey round; who
maintains the estimate.

## Annex A. Methods {#annex-a}

*Analyst:* survey, food module and recall period; sampling design;
conversion to grams; composition sources and matching; adult female
equivalents; estimators (design-based, domains of the full design). State
the secondary use of the survey microdata and its licence.


## Annex C. Biases and their direction {#annex-c}

*Analyst:* a table with the source of error, the direction of its effect on
the estimated risk and the control applied (intrahousehold distribution,
food away from home, stocks, composition, uniform fortification of the
vehicle).

```{r annex-d-energy}
#| fig-height: 3
```

## Annex F. Reference values and parameters {#annex-f}

```{r annex-f}
req <- as.data.frame(requirements)
knitr::kable(req[req$nutrient %in% p$nutrients, ],
             caption = "Requirements and upper levels used, with their source.")
shown_value <- function(v) {
  if (is.null(v)) "not set" else paste(v, collapse = ", ")
}
knitr::kable(data.frame(parameter = names(p),
                        value = vapply(p, shown_value, "")),
             caption = "Parameters of this report.")
```
